sense.text:
The disciples came to Christ privately and asked two things: “when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” Christ gave us clues, signs we have to look for to know that he is about to return and that the end of the world is near. That is what to focus on.

The earthquakes of these weeks are why this is read now: the Philippines, two in Venezuela within seconds of each other, Japan, Indonesia and California, six great shocks in under three weeks. The scriptures show what is happening on this earth. This is not a fairy tale or a story book. It is a history book, our heritage, what happened to us in the past and what is going to happen in the future. That is what prophecy is.

“For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” That is Christianity and Judaism. Those people that call themselves Jews and those that call themselves Christians come in the name of Christ and deceive many. Before Christ returns there has to be a fake religion set up in his name, and it has happened.

“And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars”: Russia and Ukraine, Lebanon, Israel, Iran, Sudan, the Congo. What we see now is going to get worse. China will go to war with Taiwan, and what Russia is doing will not stay in Ukraine; it will go further.

“See that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.” All the wars and rumours of wars, all those things, and the end is not yet.

“For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom”: that is what we see today. “And there shall be famines”: famine has begun on the earth. “And pestilences”, like the coronavirus. “And earthquakes, in divers places”: in different places. What we see in Venezuela and in all these diverse places, the earth shaking, is a sign that Christ is about to return. It could be ten years, twenty years, twenty-five, but these are the signs that he is about to return.

“All these are the beginning of sorrows.” When you see the earthquakes and the wars and all these things, this is the beginning of sorrows, and that is the time we are living in. There is much pain and sorrow coming on this earth, brothers and sisters. We do not understand sorrows as yet, but soon we will.

precepts.why:
“Behold, the plagues are sent, and shall not return again, until they come upon the earth.” The wars, the rumours of wars and the earthquakes of Matthew 24 are plagues the Lord is sending on the earth, and they shall not return until they come upon it. “The fire is kindled, and shall not be put out, till it consume the foundation of the earth.” Like an arrow “shot of a mighty archer” that “returneth not backward: even so the plagues that shall be sent upon earth shall not return again.”

“Woe is me! woe is me! who will deliver me in those days?” Ezra the prophet is on this earth right now, while these plagues are taking place. One of us might be him.

“The beginning of sorrows and great mournings”: the same beginning of sorrows Christ spoke of in Matthew 24. The plagues go into the wars, the pestilence and the famine, and the sorrows and the pain are going to get worse and worse. Great mournings: over fifteen hundred dead in Venezuela; the Palestinians mourning as they are starved out, the Lebanese mourning, the Ukrainian mothers mourning. “The beginning of famine and great death”: millions died from the coronavirus. “The beginning of wars, and the powers shall stand in fear; the beginning of evils! what shall I do when these evils shall come?” Ezra saw these things.

“Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” Amendment means judgment. The Lord is judging the nations right now with these plagues, and he is afflicting us also that are among these nations, for us to wake up. “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness”: our people will not change from their wickedness, and the nations will not repent: not Esau, not the Chinese, not the Lebanese, not the Arabs.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case”: gas prices have come down since Trump let out the reserves, and victuals, food and clothing are cheap, so everyone thinks they are in a good estate. “And even then shall evils grow upon earth.” As the evils multiply, the wars, the plagues, the pestilence, the prices of everything will multiply too, with food shortages and high demand. Victuals are not going to stay cheap forever, so buy now and put things up. That is what Trump is afraid of: that is why he is trying to make a peace deal with Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz, because the European economy and the world economy will collapse. These are the signs to look for before Christ returns, and it is not going to get better.

sense.text:
This is what God prophesied concerning Iran, America and Israel. “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them”: the Medes are Iran today, and God will stir them up against America and Israel. This literally happened back then: the Medes and Persians destroyed ancient Babylon. Everything is like a circle. The same way the Lord used the Persians and the Medes in ancient time to destroy ancient Babylon, he will use them in this time to play a role in destroying Mystery Babylon the Great, and Mystery Babylon is America and Israel; they are one.

“Which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” Trump promised Iran three hundred billion dollars, and according to this Iran does not care about that money. America killed the Ayatollah, his government, his granddaughter, and over a hundred and fifty children; no money will stop them from doing what they are going to do. You cannot buy them off the way you buy off Saudi Arabia and these other countries. This week Iran walked out of the negotiations when the vice president came to sign the peace deal, and told them to stop bombing Lebanon. God is doing this. Things are heating up, and the war is not going to stop; it is going to get worse.

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah with brimstone and fire, and ancient Babylon was not destroyed that way: the Medes and Persians conquered it from within. So the prophecy is twofold, and this is a future prophecy, not only something that happened back then.

“How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased! The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked”. The golden city is America, and it is also called the staff of the wicked. God is going to break them in the future. This is future prophecy.

“Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us.” This means the Israeli government is going to keep making war with Lebanon. After Babylon is destroyed, Lebanon will say that since you have fallen nobody has come up against us. The war in Lebanon is not going to stop, and there will be no peace there until then.

“Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming”: that is all the nations rising up against America and Israel. “It stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth”: all nations will gather together against the king of Babylon. “It hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations”: China, Europe, Russia, Iran.
“Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?” All the kings of the nations will say this to America and Israel when they are brought down.
“Thy pomp is brought down to the grave”: all the pride that America and Israel have will be brought down to the grave. That is future prophecy.

precepts.why:
Habakkuk proves that the war in Lebanon will not stop. “Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him”: that drink is the cup the Lord gave to Babylon and made all nations drink of, a cup of affliction, death and destruction. That is Israel and America, oppressing the people over there. “That thou mayest look on their nakedness!”: looking on their shame.

“Thou art filled with shame for glory”: that is how all the nations look at the Israeli government and America, while they are over there raping Palestinians, men and women. “Drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be uncovered”: let your nasty stinking foreskin be uncovered. Now you have to drink that same cup you made the Lebanese drink, the Palestinians drink, and all nations drink. “The cup of the Lord’s right hand shall be turned unto thee, and shameful spewing shall be on thy glory.”

Then God says why: “For the violence of Lebanon shall cover thee”. Because of all the murdering and bombing in Lebanon. Netanyahu says they will not stop bombing Lebanon and need to get rid of Hezbollah, but God says Lebanon will not be destroyed. They may take little pieces of land, but they will not take Lebanon, and they will be hated for what they are doing there. “Because of men’s blood”: it is going to get so intensified, and the Israeli government will do a lot of killing in Lebanon, “and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.”

“Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and Libanus”. Libanus is Lebanon. God will have them “turn themselves one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.”

That repayment is because of what they did to us, going into slavery. Lebanon in the Bible is called Tyrus, and also Tyre and Zidon: Tyre the upper part and Zidon the lower, southern Lebanon, the part the Israeli government occupies right now. When you read Joel about Tyre and Zidon, that is Lebanon. Originally Hamitic tribes occupied that land; today it is Arabs, who conquered them and took the land. What the Hamitic tribes did to us, the Arabs did the same, so God will gather the nations to pay them back for what they have done to us.

So the earthquakes, the wars and all this are signs that Christ is about to come back.

sense.text: “That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.” This explains what being born again is.
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” The Lord says we must be born again.

“The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” The wind that bloweth where it listeth is the word of God; you do not know who the word of God is going to affect. That is every last one of us in here. We heard the truth, we heard that sound, that call, and it activated us. We are like the Lord’s secret agents, his sleeper cells on the earth: you only have to hear a certain trigger word behind you and you activate. This Bible is the activation. You wake up to this truth, and now you are born.

precepts.why:
“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers”. “And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it”, whether you turn to the left or to the right.

That word behind you is the sound of John 3:8. The sound thereof is “This is the way, walk ye in it”: the word of God. That word you hear is how you are born, how you are born of the spirit. And it comes with the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, which is where this class goes: a brother is born for adversity.

sense.text:
“A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.” This goes, first, into you and your brothers going through things together. But it also means that when a brother is born into this truth, he will have to go through adversity.

Many of us come to the truth and ask, why are these things happening to me, I am following Jesus? But all of us prayed for God to use us. Did he use the apostles, Paul, the prophets? They suffered and went through pain. When you pray, God use me, you are asking to be hated by this world. When you ask God to increase your faith, he has to put you through things and then step in and work a miracle; that is how you learn to trust him. When you ask to be strong and unmovable in this truth, how does a fighter become strong? He has to fight. You ask for strength and God gives you difficulties to make you strong; ask for wisdom and he gives you problems to solve; ask for courage and he gives you dangers to overcome, the enemy in front of you when things get real; ask for love and he gives you troubled people to help. Your prayers are answered. Some never knew sickness or loss until they came to this truth, and ask why it is happening now that they serve God. This is why: we were born for adversity.

precepts.why:
Why does a brother have to go through adversity once he comes to this truth, learns he is an Israelite and starts keeping the commandments? “Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey”.

When you depart from evil, that is what John calls being born again: you wake up to this truth and say, let me serve God. And you make yourself a prey, a target. Everybody hates you and everybody is against you, but the number one enemy is also against you: Satan. Once you change your life and try to do right, Satan says, this one is trying to change, and he comes for you. Here comes the ex you haven’t seen in five years, who was fronting on you when you were in the world; now that you have departed from iniquity she is like a lion, hitting you up. Satan’s job is to destroy every last one of us that is born, every one the word of God wakes up and calls to this truth.

Paul says, “For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.” He was alive under the old covenant, and then he learned Christ. “And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death.”

Sin revived means that when you come to serve God, after a while you are dealing with things you were not dealing with before: why am I dealing with this demon, where did this come from? Sin does revive. That is Satan trying to destroy you. He is coming for you, brothers.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. That is the hunter, and we are the prey. He is trying to devour those of us that depart from iniquity. This is the spiritual demon, not his children the white men. His children do the same, but this is that old demon, the one in your head that you cannot see. Now he tries you with your lusts, the things you battle inside with, and it becomes really sinful and really hard. As you learn the law of Christ, sin revives and you keep fighting these demons, because now you are aware of it and you have changed your life, and Satan’s job is to pull you out of this truth and back into your sins. That is why it gets harder. It is warfare, by our own lusts and enticement, through temptation, affliction and tribulation.

“Whom resist stedfast in the faith”: when those lusts and desires come, resist him steadfast in this truth; resist the devil and he shall flee. “Knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.” The same lusts and fights, the same afflictions you go through, your brother is going through. Don’t think you alone are struggling; Satan is coming for all of us. That affliction also goes into persecution, when he uses his children: imprisonment, jail, all of that.

“But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” We must suffer. None of us is getting the kingdom of heaven unless we suffer; we all have to go through that fire. And suffering makes you perfect. Some have had a hard life, some are sick and the doctor says they will die, some had children leave or die, some had a spouse leave and take the kids, some are in financial difficulty: God says when you suffer it makes you perfect, stablishes you, strengthens you. So don’t ask God why. You told God you want to be strong, and he says, I will make bad things happen to you, and that is what will make you strong. Even in the gym you do not become strong without pain, and the more you work, the more you can bear it. “To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.”

Job is the example of being born for adversity: he that turns to righteousness becomes a prey, and the adversary the devil seeks whom he may devour. Satan means adversary. The same way he tempted Christ, he does to every last one of us.

“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan said he came “From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” He rules the earth and goes about looking for whom he may devour, which brother is righteous. Satan has a role to play: to tempt us, to bring affliction and pain and try us, and as we fight him it makes us perfect in the sight of God.

“Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man”. Satan answered, “Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” A hedge is protection, and the hedge is angels: bodyguards who stop Satan at the door because the Lord told them to protect you, like the angels and chariots around Elisha. Our children are under our hedge, so sometimes Satan has not come for them yet, but when that hedge is removed he will. “Thou hast blessed the work of his hands”: what you have in this world, the Lord blessed you with, though he makes the sun shine on the good and the evil, and the wicked are blessed to their detriment.

“Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” The Lord removed the hedge from Job, and that will happen to all of us from time to time; that is the affliction, the pain. The Lord will not allow you to be tempted more than you are able to bear: your car may be totalled or your house burn down and nothing happens to you. Everything that happens to us in this truth has a reason behind it. Satan does not make a move without the Lord allowing it. The Lord builds you up, then allows something to happen to try you and see what you will do with what you have learned, like when brothers rose up in 2018 saying the Sabbath is in the morning and some went back into the world.

Then Satan attacked: “the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away”. The Sabeans are the Ethiopians, or the Somalians. The Chaldeans, the Babylonians, “made out three bands, and fell upon the camels”, “The fire of God is fallen from heaven”, all from Satan. He uses people: when somebody comes at you, or tries to get you fired on your job, it is Satan using that person. Job lost his cattle, his servants, his whole financial standing, all in one day; then a great wind “smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead.”

Job “fell down upon the ground, and worshipped, And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Christ said if you are not willing to lose everything you cannot be his disciple; that is the state of mind we have to have. “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly”: he did not say, God, why me, why did you kill my sons and take my riches. It hurt him, but when bad things happen we have to know the Lord allowed it and trust that there is a reason. When Job did not break, Satan asked to touch his flesh and make him sick. Some of us are sick right now, and that is Satan, but whether we come through it is up to the Lord; sometimes he allows sickness to build our faith, because when the doctor says you have a year to live is when you pray the most, and when the Lord heals you, your faith increases and you learn the power of prayer. Job’s life is a template for what each one of us will have to go through.

A city “full of all good things”, whose entrance is narrow, between a fire on the right hand and a deep water on the left, “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That city is the kingdom of heaven, and only one man can go there at once: each of us has to go through it ourselves. The most a brother can do is bring you the scriptures, but whether it is imprisonment, sickness or the loss of a family member, you have to go through it and bear it.

“If he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?” Those dangers are the pain and affliction Job went through, and we all have to go through it. “Even so also is Israel’s portion.” That is our portion, those of us who wake up to who we are.

“When Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done. Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail”. Before, the kingdom was given to us; since Adam sinned we have to work for it, suffer and fight Satan to get the kingdom. “They are but few and evil”: whether we live fifty, seventy or eighty years, all that time we are fighting Satan. It is “very painful”. We as a people have been through a lot of pain, and that pain is good because it molds you and makes you who you are; a brother who has never been through anything, still living in his mama’s house, has been done a disservice.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was when Adam was ruling before he fell, when all the sons of God, all Israelites, were immortal. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”. Brothers, this is the condition of the battle, and all of us born upon the earth have to fight it. “That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said”: if you allow Satan to overcome you, you will suffer damnation, hell. “But if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say”: the kingdom of heaven, and that is what we all want.

Read again with verse 12, the entrance is narrow, “full of sorrow and travail”, and very painful. Do not think you will be an Israelite and just teach on the street and that is it. Things are going to get turned up in your personal life and on every level, even from the government.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion”. God says we must be in pain. That pain is affliction and tribulation, all the bad things that happen to us when we come to serve the Lord. And while we are going through that pain we still have to labour to bring forth. Even though bad things are happening to us, we still labour.

We pray, God use us, use IUIC to push thy word to the four corners of the earth. Here is what it means for God to use you, so pray with understanding. “Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.”

“But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.” Why would you be brought before kings and nobles? Because you are in chains: arrested, locked up, labelled a terrorist. Christ told Peter that when he was old he would be carried where he did not want to go. Jeremiah was locked in the dungeon. If you want God to use you, you might go to jail.

“Take no thought how or what ye shall speak”, “For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.” That is God using you, even while you are bound and brought before nobles. “And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death”: people will betray you. “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.” If you want to be loved by everybody, this is not the place for you. The only people who will love you are those who love God, and this world does not love God. Christ said they hated him first, so they will hate you.

This is Paul, whom God used. “In labours more abundant, in stripes above measure”: he was beaten above measure because God was using him. “In prisons more frequent”: he went to jail on the regular. “Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one”: that is a lot of lashes, just from the Jews. “Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned”, when he died and came back alive. “Thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep”.

“In perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen”, “in perils among false brethren”: fake, phony brothers. “In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.” Why was Paul going through all this? Because he turned to righteousness, and Satan was coming for him. Besides all that, “the care of all the churches.”

“If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.” In Damascus the governor kept the city “with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me”, to lock Paul up for teaching the word of God. “And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.” It was not his time yet, but that was Satan too, trying to kill Paul. So understand why it happens: you asked God for strength and asked him to use you; don’t question why. It hurts, but it is good, to make us perfect.

God “comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble”. “For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ”: we will get our prize.

“And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer”. The key thing is that we have to endure that suffering, because we all are going to suffer. It starts on the personal level, Satan coming at the things in your flesh the Lord wants to get out of you, and then it goes to the next level, where the dragon makes war with us, Esau comes against us and the government labels us a hate group. “As ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.”

In Asia “we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life”. “But we had the sentence of death in ourselves”: Paul and the brothers with him had made up their minds to die for the Lord. Christ said if you are not willing to lose your life you cannot be his disciple. As soldiers in Christ we have to take our minds to that level. “That we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead”: they knew the Lord would bring them back.

“Ye also helping together by prayer for us”: when bad things happen we have to fast and pray; that is our power right now. Paul thanks them because God delivered them through their prayers when they thought they were about to be killed.

“Your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure”. The persecutions our forefathers and the believers in Christ went through are coming again. The key thing is that we must endure; we cannot give up when things get bad.

“Which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which ye also suffer”. The righteous judgment of God is the affliction we go through; that is how the Lord tells who is worthy: you go through the affliction and endure it. “Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you”: those who bring affliction on us, God will pay back. Don’t worry.

“Remember my judgment: for thine also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for thee.” You see a brother sick, a sister’s house burned down, a brother who lost his son, and some disconnect: it is not you going through it, so you don’t feel it. But your time is coming, when tribulation and affliction come on you. Yesterday for me, tomorrow for you.

So when brothers go through things, we have to pray for each other and feel what that man is going through. When one suffers, we all suffer; bear each other’s burdens. We all have to go through that fire.

“Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us”: everybody has that one sin that is hard to fight. “And let us run with patience the race that is set before us”: you cannot run it fast.

“Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame”. He could have called angels and killed everybody, but he endured being nailed to a cross, the Son of God letting the people he created beat him. “For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.” Christ’s suffering is our example. Weariness starts in the mind, because nobody wants to suffer, go to prison, be sick or die, so some give up and go back to the world and make an excuse.

“Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.” We are all being built up, but we have not resisted unto blood as yet. When Christ said he that denies me I will deny, it is about when your life is on the line: they tell you that you are going to jail for the next thirty years for teaching the word, and you start thinking about your wife and kids, and that you will never taste vagina again. You might die in prison; your life on this earth is over, behind bars for teaching the word of God while they label you a hate group. Not denying Christ while you are being persecuted and tortured, as Peter and them were: that is what this is about, and that is where we all have to bring our minds. Some will remember this class.

“My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him”: to faint is to give up. When bad things happen, don’t give up. “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” Why are bad things happening to me? Because God loves you. Every last one of us he says is his son, he has to scourge and put through things to make us strong and perfect. “If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons”: only if you endure it. “But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” If you are not going through anything, you belong to Satan, or the Lord is not ready for you yet.

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous”. This also goes into the leaders correcting the brothers: it does not feel good. “Nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” You come out better and bring forth fruit.

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees”: when things go bad or you get corrected, you hang your hands down and are sad all the time. “Lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.” Don’t go back to the world after four or five years in this truth because of correction. Let that correction heal you; it was meant to hurt. Don’t sit and listen to Satan telling you they hate you.

“Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord”: you could end up hating the one who corrected you, and you will not see God carrying hatred toward your brothers. “Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled”. “As Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Bitterness is like Esau selling his birthright. A brother who gives up his rank, saying I don’t want to be a captain or an officer anymore, I can’t deal with this responsibility, is no different from Esau giving up his birthright; it is like spitting in Christ’s face, and he will not get it back. If you need help, ask for help.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away”.

Many of us are learning these scriptures, learning what Christ will do when he returns, with the Holy Spirit on us on certain levels. Then some talk about leaving IUIC because somebody corrected them. You learned all of this and now you are out? Get your mind right. When correction comes, don’t let bitterness destroy you inside, and don’t let Satan whisper in your mind to take you out of this truth. When those thoughts come, realize that is Satan.

For those making videos about why they left IUIC: “Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists”. Antichrist means you are against Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us”. Historically, there were men among the apostles who left and taught different doctrines, that the resurrection had already happened, or that you had to come back to the law of Moses. It also goes into brothers today. The Lord sent us among each other for a purpose; leaving is telling the Lord to hell with you and giving him the middle finger, going to do your own thing.

“For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us”: a brother who is real will not just leave because the Deacon offended him. “But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” It is good when brothers leave, because it shows who is with you. Shed no tears. When tribulation and affliction arise, many will not stick around, because they did not take these lessons seriously.

“Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” We have to endeavour, to fight, to keep the unity because Satan will try to bring disunity. We will have problems with each other; a brother might offend you. Christ told us how to deal with it: if a brother offends you, go and deal with it with him. If you were really about this truth you would not leave; you would fix the problem and continue with your brothers.

“Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long”. Back then they were killed all the day long for Christ’s sake, and it is going to happen again. The point is that nothing should separate you from the love of Christ: no tribulation, no offence, nothing from nobody should make you stop keeping the commandments or stop building with the men the Lord sent you to build with.

“For there is a shame that bringeth sin; and there is a shame which is glory and grace. Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.” You cannot let your reverence for anybody cause you to fall. A man you like goes through his trials, fails when the Lord tests him, and says he is out; do not leave with him because you like him. You are supposed to be in this truth because you love the Lord.

“Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man’s work shall be made manifest”. The gold, silver and precious stones are the brothers who go through the fire, the trials, and are not destroyed. The hay and stubble are those who cannot endure the fire of affliction, persecution or even offences, and give up.

“For the day shall declare it”: that day is tribulation, when the fire comes, and it will tell what kind of work you are, the righteous brother or the unrighteous, gold or hay. “Because it shall be revealed by fire”. Fire is that affliction and persecution, and fire brings the impurities out of you. If you are hay and stubble you will be burnt up: you will up and leave. The gold goes through the fire and the pain, and comes out on top, stronger and better.

You prayed, Lord help me love my neighbour as myself, and then God allowed your neighbour to offend you, and you are still mad and won’t forgive. The Lord is answering your prayer: he made the situation arise so you would apply it. That is how the Most High works.

“Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.” God chose us, and for God to choose you, you have to go through the furnace of affliction. God is not choosing any of us unless we go through affliction. We have to prove to him we are worthy, and that means he puts us through things that hurt, even among each other.

You pray for strength, he makes bad things happen to make you strong. You pray for faith, he makes you go through things to build your faith. You pray to love your neighbour, he lets your neighbour offend you to see if you apply that law. That is how the Lord proves who is real; those who are not real will faint and give up.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” To be acceptable means to be chosen. The same way gold is tried in the fire, if you are acceptable God puts you through adversity: tribulation, persecution, sickness, as Job went through. Every son he chooses he has to chasten, to make us perfect. He is proving whether you love him: you say you love me, deal right with your brother; you say you love me, endure the temptations I send your way.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Everyone in here came to serve the Lord, so prepare your soul: bad things are going to happen in your life. Why? Because he that turns to righteousness makes himself a prey, as with Job. Your adversary the devil, the accuser of the brethren, is coming hard. Christ told Peter that Satan desired to sift him.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” When Satan comes and bad things happen, keep enduring and do not make haste. Some sisters going through problems in their marriage talk about leaving; trouble and affliction come through your spouse too. Don’t make haste, unless he is a crackhead who won’t stop, or he is beating the crap out of you and trying to kill you; then leave until he fixes his stuff. When things get bad and serious, the fake and phony say they are out, and the Lord is showing who is fake and who loves him.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.” When you are sick, when your child died, when you lost your house or are in prison, it is only you and the Lord, so learn to cleave to him. In the end you will increase: brothers whose wives left and took the kids went through the fire, and the Most High blessed them. Everything is the Lord trying us; the sister or brother who offended you was Satan jumping on them to try you.

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Sometimes we will be brought very low. “Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him”: trust in God, not in Malachiyah. “Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.”

“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you”. The things we go through are that fire, and it is to try us. When bad things happen, you are being tried. Don’t act like something strange happened to you, as if you don’t understand that Satan is coming for you.

“But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.” “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye”: if they call us a hate group and persecute us because we teach that Jesus Christ is black and that we are the Israelites, we are to be happy, “for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you”.

“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations”: different kinds of temptations, and we count it joy. “Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.” Bad things happen to try whether you believe or not: will you trust in God or will you leave? That is why that sister or brother offended you, to see how you deal with it. “But let patience have her perfect work”.

“We glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience”. When you go through bad things it teaches you to wait on the Lord. “And patience, experience”: the only way to become strong and gain experience in this truth is through tribulation; if you have not been through anything, you lack experience. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed.” You have to go through tribulations to become stronger.

“Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.” As we go through things, we have to be strong in the Lord. “Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” Satan is coming to destroy you, and the whole armour is the only way to survive. “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.”

“That ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.” It does not say you won’t fall. A warrior falls, but he gets back up and stays standing; sometimes you do everything and still fall, and you still have to stand. “Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth”, with the laws, “and having on the breastplate of righteousness”.

“Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.” Faith, your belief, is the number one weapon. Christ prayed for Peter that his faith fail not, because even if you fall, you can get back up because you believe. And “Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit”.

We were born for adversity. Don’t ask God for strength without understanding that you are going to go through things.
